dosing_regimen.source_excerpt: protocolSection.armsInterventionsModule.interventions and armGroups: "Crisaborole 2%" "Crisaborole 2% ointment applied once daily (QD)" "Vehicle" "Vehicle ointment applied once daily (QD)" "Crisaborole 2%" "Crisaborole ointment 2%" "Vehicle" "Vehicle ointment" "EXPERIMENTAL" "PLACEBO_COMPARATOR" "The ISGA is a 5-point scale (range 0 to 4), reflecting a global assessment of AD severity based on erythema, induration/papulation, and oozing/crusting." "Participants identified as responders during the OL period were randomized to receive vehicle applied topically once daily (QD) for 52 weeks in the double-blind (DB) maintenance period." "Participants identified as responders during the OL period were randomized to receive crisaborole 2% ointment applied topically QD for 52 weeks in the DB maintenance period." -- The registry intervention entries identify the two QD maintenance interventions; percentages are the crisaborole product strength shown in the trial protocol. Run-in and flare-rescue BID use is described separately in the protocol and is not represented as an extra CT.gov intervention entry. Placebo status follows the CT.gov arm classifications (EXPERIMENTAL versus PLACEBO_COMPARATOR); both QD arm descriptions state 52 weeks.

alpha_split.method: Step-down closed testing; significance requires the preceding endpoint in sequence to be significant
Bonferroni; no testing order among subgroups; significance claim only after the first three endpoints are significant

method_citations: SAP 5.1.1: flare-free maintenance to first flare; number of flare-free days over 52 weeks; number of flares over 52 weeks; then five pruritus response maintenance subgroups. The first three use alpha 0.05; each subgroup uses Bonferroni-adjusted alpha 0.01.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: 5.1 Hypotheses and Decision Rules; 5.1.1 Statistical Decision Rules for Multiple Comparisons: "The primary objective is to establish the superiority of a crisaborole QD to a vehicle QD;" "flare-free period at a significance level of 0.05 (2-sided, log-rank test)." "A step-down closed testing procedure and Bonferroni’s method will be used for Type I error" "control for testing the primary endpoint and the key secondary endpoints." "Flare-free maintenance up until the onset of the first flare during the DB period." "Number of flare-free days over 52 weeks." "Number of flares over 52 weeks." "Pruritus response maintenance up until the onset of the first flare (ISGA ≥2), defined" "performed for 5 responder subgroups:" "The statistical significance can be claimed for a given endpoint in the sequence only if the" "prior endpoint in the sequence is significant." "For the endpoints of 1-3, the significance level" "is 0.05." "For pruritus response maintenance, Bonferroni’s method is used to adjust the" "significance level." "The significance level is 0.01 for each subgroup, there is no testing order." "Only the subgroup with p-value ≤0.01 can claim significance after the primary endpoint and" "other two secondary endpoints are statistically significant." "3." "4." -- Steps 1-3 are the stated fixed sequence; the five subgroup tests share step 4 because the SAP specifies no testing order among them, and each has Bonferroni-adjusted alpha 0.01. These entries preserve the SAP subgroup labels rather than forcing them onto fewer registry endpoint references. The alpha_split first-group n_endpoints value of 3 is the count of SAP-listed efficacy endpoints numbered 1 through 3.
